..
Isolated showers and thunderstorms are expected tonight and tomorrow
morning for Guam and Rota with shower coverage becoming scattered 
over Tinian and Saipan. Shower coverage will become scattered for all
islands by tomorrow afternoon as light and variable winds allow 
island effect showers to develop over at least Guam and Rota. Monday 
night through Wednesday, dry weather will persist with very gradually
increasing westerlies pushing any island effect showers offshore. By
Wednesday night, a developing tropical disturbance to the northeast 
will bring increased moisture into the Marianas with breezy 
conditions developing Thursday night or Friday. This disturbance will
be monitored closely for potential impacts to the Marianas. Models 
currently indicate it drifting north of the Marianas with a monsoon 
tail bringing potentially heavy precipitation, particularly to 
Tinian and Saipan. However, high uncertainty remains whether the 
strongest part of the monsoon tail sits over the Marianas or over the
far northern CNMI. A hydrologic outlook may be necessary in the 
coming days depending on the track and intensity of this disturbance.

Marine...
Light and variable winds will prevail through Monday. Seas around
3 feet will remain until Wednesday evening before starting to 
increase due to an expected tropical disturbance developing to the
northeast and its associated monsoon inflow shifting north into 
the Marianas. The risk of rip currents is currently low along all
reefs as only a very small southwest swell and east-northeast swell
remain. Seas may become hazardous to small craft by Thursday, with
the surf potentially becoming hazardous as well. Isolated 
thunderstorms will be possible through Monday and then again by 
Wednesday night through the end of the forecast period.

Eastern Micronesia...
Similar to yesterday, rainfall was the biggest forecast challenge as
the region remains on the southern edge of the deeper moisture.
Majuro has seen the "best" coverage of showers as they're closest to
the trough (which stretches from Utirik to 9N180). Some of the
showers have been at least moderately heavy as after one such shower
earlier Majuro dropped from 87 degrees to 82 degrees, and they remain
cooler at 83 degrees currently. As for rainfall potential, Majuro 
is on the edge of the convection, with models showing decreased 
potential for Monday into Tuesday, before potential increases once 
again. As such, the forecast was trended in that direction.

Farther south and west, both Pohnpei and Kosrae has seen little in 
the way of shower activity, with abundant mid to high level cloud 
cover offering some relief, as temperatures this afternoon were in 
the mid 80s. Given this being a second day of more convective debris
than actual shower coverage, rainfall probabilities were dropped to 
30 percent for tonight and Monday. for Monday night onward, look for 
just isolated shower coverage with probabilities in the 10 to 20 
percent range.

As for marine conditions, look for light to gentle winds to prevail
with seas holding in the 3 to 5 foot range.

Western Micronesia...
The monsoon trough remains the dominant feature in the region. The
trough is located 10N130E and extends eastward through the region 
and enters Eastern Micronesia near 10N155E. This feature is producing
scattered to numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms, with the 
strongest showers near 10N. These showers are most prevalent near 
Yap, and some showers over the northern portions of Palau and Chuuk 
waters. The monsoon trough is expected to remain quasi-stationary. 
This feature is expected to remain through most of next week. 
Altimetry shows combined seas between 3 and 5 feet. Winds are 
expected to be light to moderate. Sea conditions are expected to 
remain benign.
